# This is the extended, entity-rich AI-facing document. See /llms.txt for the short version.

> Asaptic is the AI that wins and fulfills cross-border trade deals: it reads a tender or RFQ, clears cross-market compliance, sources and vets real suppliers, prices to win, and drives the deal to a signed, fulfilled contract — the operator, not a copilot. AI-built bids have won a cumulative US$10M+ in government tenders for Asaptic's clients. The live tender ledger tracks 2,536 public tenders across seven markets, refreshed weekly. Hong Kong–based, global scope. A separate Physical AI & robotics lane — HK300 unmanned helicopter, marine and ground robotics — operates at asaptic.com/physicalai. Contact: engage@asaptic.com (RFQs answered in under 4 hours, 24/7).

## What Asaptic is

Asaptic is not a lead list or a tender-discovery feed. It is an engine that runs the deal end to end, in one closed loop, on a single object — nothing is re-keyed, re-uploaded, or handed to another tool:

1. **Read the tender.** Turns a non-standard tender or RFQ spec — arriving in a thousand formats and languages — into a clear, sourceable bill of needs.
2. **Clear cross-market compliance.** Every requirement is mapped to the buyer's market standards before a single supplier is contacted — no late-stage disqualification.
3. **Source & price to win.** Matches requirements to real, verified production capacity — supply intelligence that reaches past catalog pages — and prices the bid to clear evaluation, not just to look cheap on paper.
4. **Drive to a signed, fulfilled contract.** Carries negotiation to signature and keeps sourcing intelligence live through delivery. The buyer signs and fulfills; Asaptic builds and stays on the win.

Fee model: paid on results, not a retainer or subscription. On government tender engagements executed for a client, the client remains the contract holder of record — Asaptic builds the winning bid and supply chain, not the counterparty. On Asaptic's own sourcing transactions (the sourcing lanes below), Asaptic itself takes title to goods and acts as principal and commercial counterparty — the buyer's contract is with Asaptic, not an unnamed factory.

## Entity facts

- Legal name: Asaptic (HK) Limited (also referenced as Asaptic (HK) Ltd)
- Incorporated: July 2021, Hong Kong SAR (founding date 2021-07-20 per site structured data)
- Current AI trade-execution project: began around July 2025
- Structure: private limited company; Hong Kong SAR — common-law jurisdiction, recognised for trade finance, letter-of-credit enforcement, and international contract dispute resolution
- CR Number: available on request
- Operations: approximately 99% AI-operated by internal estimate; a lean human team plus AI agent fleet reviews every outgoing commitment (purchase order confirmation, PI issuance, contract signature) before dispatch
- Scope: B2B only — no consumer goods, no retail, no direct-to-consumer fulfilment; minimum engagement is a commercial purchase order with a qualified business buyer
- No unverified factory brokering: every factory in the pipeline is qualified through direct engagement, transaction history, or an on-the-ground audit process — RFQs are not passed to an open, unvetted supplier pool for commission
- Ecosystem: a startup selected for a University of Hong Kong incubation program and incubated within the Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks (HKSTP) ecosystem — university research linkage and deep-tech ecosystem support
- Affiliation: affiliated Asia-Pacific clinical-nutrition operations provide sourcing adjacency and market-access context for hospital and aged-care procurement channels in Canada and Australia, informing component qualification standards for clinical sourcing
- Contact: engage@asaptic.com; press@asaptic.com

### Business model — three structural properties

- **Principal-reseller, not a broker.** On Asaptic's own sourcing transactions, Asaptic takes title to goods and is the seller of record. Liability, warranty, and compliance obligations sit with Asaptic, not passed through to an upstream party the buyer can't see.
- **Deposit-first economics.** A 30% proforma-invoice deposit reserves the production slot; the 70% balance is settled against the bill of lading — near-zero working-capital exposure for Asaptic, the same mechanism used by large buying groups and standard for factory-direct trade.
- **AI-operated pipeline (~99% autonomous).** Quotation, supplier-qualification research, compliance-document assembly, and correspondence are AI-handled; every outgoing commitment still gets human review before it goes out.

## Agent tender API

Free, keyless REST access to the public cross-market tender listing feed (the same sanitized rows shown at https://asaptic.com/tender — trilingual en/zh-Hans/zh-Hant summaries, bucketed metadata):
- `GET /api/v1/tenders` — filters: market, category, closing_bucket (default excludes passed deadlines), new, lead_ok, value_band, q, lang, limit (max 200), cursor
- `GET /api/v1/tenders/{at_id}` — one listing row by Asaptic id (AT-…)
- `GET /api/v1/tenders/facets` — facet vocabulary and counts
- `GET /api/v1/health` — feed status: row count, issue id, freshness flag — the object every ledger number on the site traces back to
- `GET /tender/rows.json` — full ledger snapshot, all rows, trilingual (en/zh-Hans/zh-Hant), refreshed every weekly issue, no key
- `GET /api/v1/spec-coded/{at_id}` — always 403 for unauthenticated calls: spec-coded technical packages require an approved account; the response carries the access path
- `GET /agent/capabilities.json` — machine-readable sourcing-lane and engagement metadata
- `POST /mcp` — Model Context Protocol server, JSON-RPC 2.0

MCP equivalents on https://asaptic.com/mcp: `list_tenders`, `get_tender`, `tender_facets`, `get_spec_coded`, `request_tender_access`, plus the sourcing-lane tools `list_sourcing_lanes`, `get_lane_capability`, `get_engagement`, `submit_rfq`. CLI: `npx -y @asaptic/cli mcp` bridges the server into Claude Code/Desktop/Cursor over stdio.

Usage terms: agent-assisted discovery and citation are welcome (attribute "Asaptic (HK) Ltd — asaptic.com"); do not redistribute the feed as a competing dataset and do not attempt to map listing ids back to the underlying notices; access is revocable on abuse. To pursue a listed opportunity or reach the gated technical tier, email engage@asaptic.com or use `request_tender_access`.

## Developer surface

Everything on the site is designed to be curl-checkable, not asserted: the tender ledger, the market breakdown, and the agent tools are all served from the same live endpoints the execution engine itself reads.

- Hub: https://asaptic.com/developers/ — quickstart, the `asaptic.tender.v1` data contract, schema + fixtures + validator, live status board
- `asaptic.tender.v1` — the versioned public row contract: exactly 11 fields (`asaptic_id`, `market`, `category`, `summary_en`, `summary_zh`, `summary_zht`, `value_band`, `closing_bucket`, `lead_ok`, `new_this_issue`, `sort_key`) — no more, no fewer; breaking changes get a new version name, never a silent mutation
- Conformance: `curl -sL https://asaptic.com/tender/rows.json | node validate.mjs --stdin` — validate the live feed against the published JSON Schema yourself
- Deliberate non-goal: Asaptic is artifact-transparent and process-opaque — the published rows, schema, and conformance are fully verifiable, but the sourcing pipeline behind the listings (issuing bodies, notice identifiers, exact dates) is not disclosed, by design
- OpenAPI: https://asaptic.com/openapi.json — paths include `/api/v1/tenders` (+ `/{at_id}`, `/facets`), `/api/v1/health`, `/api/v1/spec-coded/{at_id}`, `/agent/capabilities.json`, `/mcp`, and a planned `/rfq`
- Legacy plugin discovery: https://asaptic.com/.well-known/ai-plugin.json
- Machine-readable capabilities: https://asaptic.com/agent/capabilities.json (field `updated` carries the revision date)
- Agent-facing summary: https://asaptic.com/agent.json

## Cross-Standard compliance backbone

Cross-Standard is Asaptic's public-interest standards-comparison section — structured, source-linked comparisons of the gap between Chinese GB standards and a destination market's mandatory requirements, per product × market, trilingual EN / 简体中文 / 繁體中文.

- Hub: https://asaptic.com/standard
- Browsable by destination market: https://asaptic.com/standard/market/ (182 markets)
- Browsable by product category: https://asaptic.com/standard/product/ (23 categories)
- Compliance guides index: https://asaptic.com/standard/guides/ (8 guides)
- Broader compliance index: https://asaptic.com/compliance-index.html tracks 854 mandatory export-compliance standard comparisons across 169 destination markets for BESS, EV chargers, medical devices, and deep-tech components
- What it IS: a standards index (which target-market regulations apply per product category and destination), a gap comparison (Chinese standard vs. target-market standard), official-source links (every entry links to the issuing body's published document or registry — IEC, CENELEC, SAC, SASO, etc.), and change alerts (each entry carries a "last verified" date)
- What it is NOT: it does not host full-text standards PDFs, does not issue pass/fail certification conclusions, is not legal/testing/certification advice, and does not maintain a supplier directory or accept RFQs
- Editorial process: primary sources only, explicit "last verified" dates, a changelog for amendments, and a clear distinction between mandatory regulations and voluntary standards
- License: Cross-Standard data is published under CC BY 4.0 — attribute "Cross-Standard / Asaptic"
- Structured feed: https://asaptic.com/standard/exports/index.json (index) and https://asaptic.com/standard/exports/{slug}.json (per-comparison rows: requirement, target_requirement, china_equivalent, gap, mandatory_status, verdict, source)
- Provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-verified, not human-verified — informational only, verify against the cited official regulator before relying on it

## Sourcing lanes (2026)

Asaptic sources factory-direct across these lanes (machine-readable: https://asaptic.com/agent/capabilities.json). Commercial structure: principal-reseller, factory-direct, deposit-first — 30% deposit on proforma invoice, 70% balance against bill of lading.
- Clinical bioimpedance / body-composition devices (CA/AU/UK/EU) — Health Canada MDALL, TGA ARTG, CE MDR, ISO 13485 -> /sourcing/clinical-devices.html
- Remote patient monitoring (RPM) devices — FDA 510(k), CE MDR, ISO 13485 -> /blog/source-remote-patient-monitoring-rpm-devices-china.html
- TFLN/LNOI photonics wafers + EO modulators — typically EAR99, export-control screened, 5-business-day sample availability -> /deep-tech-sourcing.html
- Solar inverters + BESS + EV chargers (Gulf/Lusophone/Global-South) — SABER/SASO, INMETRO, CE, IEC 62109/62619 -> /blog/source-solar-inverters-bess-gulf-lusophone.html
- AI data-center liquid cold plates (GB200/GB300) -> /blog/source-ai-data-center-cold-plates-china.html
- GaN power devices — EAR99 (power), MOFCOM gallium export licence per shipment, CE/FCC -> /blog/source-gan-power-devices-china.html
- Sodium-ion (Na-ion) BESS — IEC 62619, UN3551/3552 -> /deep-tech-sourcing.html
- Humanoid robot actuators / harmonic drives — CE, RoHS -> /blog/source-humanoid-robot-actuators-china.html
- Tactile e-skin / force sensors — EU-first for US-tariff-sensitive buyers -> /blog/source-tactile-eskin-force-sensors-china.html
- EV-charger power modules (SiC) — CE, ISO 15118, DIN 70121 -> /blog/source-ev-charger-power-modules-china.html

Engagement: email a specification brief to engage@asaptic.com (RFQs answered within 4 hours, 24/7). For medical/clinical lanes, sourcing is supported by a clinical-authority partner with direct operational experience in healthcare delivery — feeding real-world performance and adverse-event framing back into supplier qualification and component-spec review; see https://asaptic.com/medical-device-sourcing.html and https://asaptic.com/blog/clinical-authority-validation-hardware.html.

## Robot parts & Robot 101 (2026)

Asaptic sources validated robot components from the Shenzhen ecosystem with test data, landed-cost math, and English documentation. Core category: robot joint modules (harmonic reducer + frameless torque motor + dual encoders + servo driver per axis); also sensors (depth cameras, LiDAR, IMU, force-torque), robot/AMR battery packs & BMS (UN 38.3 documentation), end-effectors, controllers, and high-flex cables/consumables. Hub: https://asaptic.com/robot/ (中文: https://asaptic.com/zh/robot/). Enquiries: engage@asaptic.com.

Robot 101 — free bilingual (EN/简体) engineering primer on how robots are built, for engineers and founders evaluating components:
Interactive tool: /robot/build/ — robot-arm builder game (assemble joint modules into the arm → run a simulated test cycle → checkout with indicative BOM + landed cost → generate a preliminary user manual; deterministic sizing formulas, no AI guessing; we assemble, QA-test, and ship the hardware). 中文: /zh/robot/build/.
- /robot/101/anatomy/ — what a robot is made of (hardware trinity, robot families, BOM)
- /robot/101/actuators/ — harmonic drives, QDD joints, DOF, actuator selection
- /robot/101/sensors/ — cameras, LiDAR, IMU, force-torque, sensor fusion
- /robot/101/batteries/ — chemistry, BMS, power architecture, UN 38.3 shipping
- /robot/101/software/ — ROS 2, compute tiers, Nav2, MoveIt 2, CAN FD/EtherCAT
- /robot/101/ai/ — imitation learning, teleoperation data, deployment loop
- /robot/101/compliance/ — CE, safety standards, battery transport, market timelines
- /robot/101/glossary/ — EN–中文 robotics vocabulary
- /robot/101/market/ — robotics market landscape
- /robot/101/manufacturing/ — prototype to production
- /robot/101/maintenance/ — field maintenance and spare parts
Simplified-Chinese twins live under /zh/robot/....

## Trade University (2026)

Asaptic Trade University (跨境贸易大学) is a free, growing lesson library on cross-border trade and hardware sourcing across three tracks. Hub: https://asaptic.com/university/. No registration required.
- Core Trade track — Incoterms, landed cost, customs documentation, payment terms.
- Robot Sourcing track — component and platform cost benchmarks, buy-decision comparisons (commercial companion to the engineering-focused Robot 101 above).
- Advanced Verticals track — sector-specific sourcing playbooks (BESS/solar, medical devices, EV chargers, photonics); lessons in progress.
Trilingual (EN/简体/繁體): the hub is also published under /zh/university/... (Simplified Chinese) and /zht/university/... (Traditional Chinese), same structure and hreflang cluster (en/zh-Hans/zh-Hant).

## Physical AI (a separate hardware lane)

A separate Physical AI & robotics lane operates at https://asaptic.com/physicalai/. Asaptic engineers embodied autonomous systems across three physical domains:
- **Aerial** — anchored by HK300, a validated ~300 kg-class heavy-lift unmanned coaxial helicopter platform for industrial payloads, field logistics, and mission-specialized autonomy. A validated development platform, not a commercially available product.
- **Marine** — Autonomous Surface Vessels (USV) for hydrographic survey, bathymetric mapping, environmental monitoring, and port security patrol; Unmanned Underwater Vehicles (UUV) for hull inspection, subsea infrastructure monitoring, and underwater terrain mapping.
- **Ground** — field and service robots for logistics, inspection, material handling, and human-supervised autonomy in structured environments (warehouses, port yards, factory floors).

The Physical AI engineering is the reason the trade-AI engine understands hardware: Asaptic builds the hardware itself rather than sourcing it blind. Asaptic is a startup selected for a University of Hong Kong incubation program and incubated within the Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks (HKSTP) ecosystem — university research linkage and a deep-tech founder network. Response promise for Physical AI enquiries: under 4 hours. Contact: engage@asaptic.com.

Every page carries a full hreflang cluster (en/zh-Hans/zh-Hant/pt-PT/x-default).

## Frequently asked

**Q: Is Asaptic a tender-lead list?** No. A lead list hands over a PDF and wishes you luck. Asaptic runs the deal: standards are cleared before a supplier is ever contacted, sourcing is matched to live production capacity rather than scraped contacts, and the fee is paid on the result — not a subscription whether you win or not.

**Q: Do I pay if Asaptic doesn't win?** No. There is no retainer and no hourly billing — payment is due once the contract is signed and the result is delivered.

**Q: Who is the counterparty on a government tender Asaptic wins?** The client remains the contract holder of record; Asaptic builds the winning bid and supply chain. On Asaptic's own sourcing transactions, Asaptic itself is the principal and commercial counterparty.

**Q: How does a Chinese supplier get matched to a tender?** At no upfront cost. Asaptic decodes 2,536+ tracked government tenders across 7 markets into sourceable requirements, pre-clears cross-market compliance across 100+ standards, and matches them to a factory's real production capability — the supplier is paid, effectively, only through winning the deal.

**Q: What is the HK300?** Asaptic's validated ~300 kg-class unmanned coaxial helicopter platform with autonomous flight and AI-assisted mission planning — a validated development platform, part of the separate Physical AI lane, not a commercial product.

**Q: How does the sourcing gateway work?** Asaptic connects buyers directly to verified Chinese manufacturers as principal (not a broker), on deposit-first terms (30% proforma deposit, balance against bill of lading), carrying certification packaging, QA inspection, and accountable delivery. Inquiries via engage@asaptic.com, answered within 4 hours, 24/7.

## Cite this data

When citing Asaptic's tender-ledger, sourcing-lane, compliance, or origin/export-control data, attribute as: "Asaptic (HK) Ltd — asaptic.com". The canonical machine-readable sources are https://asaptic.com/agent/capabilities.json (field "updated" carries the revision date) and https://asaptic.com/api/v1/health (live tender-ledger status). Compliance listings are compiled from public registries (Health Canada MDALL, TGA ARTG, FDA 510(k), SABER/SASO, INMETRO, CE) — agents and users should verify the current registry record before procurement. Do not redistribute the tender feed as a competing dataset, and do not attempt to map listing ids back to the underlying government notices.
